$comment: The status checks main's branch protection requires, kept in the repo so a change to a workflow matrix and a change to what main requires land in the same commit. EVERY check name the workflows produce must appear in exactly one of `required` or `not_required` — test/workflow-supply-chain.test.js derives the real names from .github/workflows and fails if this file has an entry no job produces (a phantom context, which makes main unmergeable by everyone) or omits one a job does produce (a real check nothing requires, which can fail while the PR still merges). Reconcile with GitHub via `node scripts/workflow-checks.js --remote`, which prints the gh command rather than running it.
$comment_strict: strict = GitHub's 'require branches to be up to date before merging'. Recorded here because the apply command PATCHes the whole required_status_checks object: omitting it would silently turn the setting off.

not_required.Analyze (actions): CodeQL's `actions` pack lints the workflow files themselves, and it runs on every PR — its findings still reach the Security tab. It is deliberately not a required context: scripts/codeql/severity-policy.json names `Analyze (javascript-typescript)` as the single blocking code-scanning context, and the `main` ruleset's code_scanning rule already gates merges on alert severity across both packs. Requiring this second context would give one policy two enforcement points that can disagree. Not an oversight — do not 'fix' it by adding it.
not_required.publish: The publish job runs only on push to main and workflow_dispatch; publish.yml has no `pull_request` trigger, so a pull request never produces this check. Requiring a context the PR event cannot produce is precisely the phantom that once left main unmergeable by everyone. It must stay unrequired.
